clue.text: Union with merit, when there's cutback in the country

parts.note: TU is the usual abbreviation for trade union

indicators.note: a cutback trims something, so the word for merit loses its final letter

parts.note: merit means value, worth

explanation.surface: Some union deal over merit pay in a country facing spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutback' takes the last letter off VALUE, leaving VALU.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuvalu is a small island nation in the Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Begin with first of mounts being favourite, showing fitness

indicators.note: one letter being something else means it is replaced by that thing

parts.note: to begin is to commence

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word mounts is wanted

parts.note: a favourite is a pet, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Advice to a rider: start on your best horse to prove you are fit.
explanation.walkthrough: One M of COMMENCE (the M given by 'first of mounts') becomes PET.
explanation.definitionFit: Competence is capability, fitness for a task.

clue.text: Coastal areas King-Emperor goes to six times

parts.note: RI stands for Rex Imperator, King and Emperor, as on old coins of British India
VI is six in Roman numerals
times as in ages or periods: eras

explanation.surface: A monarch makes repeated trips to fashionable seaside resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: A riviera is a stretch of coast popular with holidaymakers, so rivieras are coastal regions.

clue.text: Support off the ground again?

definitions.meaning: something held in reserve to support you
taken as ..., raised up once more

explanation.surface: Someone propping up a fallen thing to get it standing once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A backup is reserve support; read as two words it means lifted up again.

clue.text: London street bar with wicked gal getting sozzled

indicators.note: sozzled means very drunk, so these letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A London pub where a naughty young woman gets thoroughly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdcage Walk is a street in Westminster running beside St James's Park.

clue.text: Copper bad dog nipped — something fleshy to get teeth into

definitions.text: something fleshy to get teeth into

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a cur is a worthless mongrel
nipped means bit

explanation.surface: A police officer gets bitten by a vicious mutt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman; here it is the metal's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A cucurbit is a gourd-family fruit such as a marrow or pumpkin, with flesh to eat.

clue.text: Thus Vince embraces one, being friendly

parts.note: thus means so

indicators.note: embracing something holds it inside, so the surname wraps around the numeral

parts.note: Vince Cable is a British Liberal Democrat politician
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A politician hugging somebody shows how amiable he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sociable means enjoying company, friendly and outgoing.

clue.text: City with eight million, say, that may disappear under water

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset
eight is two cubed and a million is a hundred cubed, so each is an example of a cube

explanation.surface: A big city of eight million at risk of flooding.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is a Roman spa city in England, not the multi-million metropolis the surface implies.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath cube is a block of scented salts that dissolves away in bathwater.

clue.text: A nice ground occupied by superior traveller and settler from across the waters

indicators.note: something occupied by another has it inside, so the anagram is split around the rest
ground means crushed and reduced, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: U is the old British label for upper-class, superior
a traveller is one who roams, a roamer

explanation.surface: A pleasant piece of land is taken by a posh wanderer who has come from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A nice ground' reads as a pleasant field, but 'ground' is the anagram signal and 'occupied by' splits that anagram around the posh wanderer; U is the old upper-class label.
explanation.definitionFit: A Euro-American is someone of European descent settled in America, across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Subsequently involves Conservative in U-turn from behind?

indicators.note: a U-turn means going back the way you came, so the result reads backwards
involving something takes it in, so the abbreviation goes inside the word

parts.note: subsequently means later

explanation.surface: A Tory government reverses a policy afterwards, a backside matter.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes into LATER to make LATCER, and 'in U-turn' turns that around.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectal means relating to the rectum, the rear end, so it is a playful sense of coming from behind.

clue.text: One runs second computer attachment

parts.note: a printer is a device attached to a computer

explanation.surface: Someone runs a second peripheral off a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter is an athlete who races, one who runs fast over short distances.

clue.text: Part of engine bad, inadequate — trouble car rescue team to return

indicators.note: returning goes back, so the whole string of pieces reads backwards
inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: bad means rotten
trouble means rub, as in 'there's the rub'
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British breakdown rescue service

explanation.surface: A motorist's engine breaks down and the recovery crew must come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' cuts ROTTEN to ROTTE; ROTTE + RUB + RAC is then turned back by 'to return'.
explanation.definitionFit: A carburettor mixes fuel and air in a petrol engine, so it is an engine component.

clue.text: What you encounter in nuclear theory is dull

definitions.text: What you encounter in nuclear theory
definitions.meaning: the letters of 'nuclear theory' hold the word EARTH within them, so earth is bound inside that phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The first part is a cryptic description: look inside 'nuclEAR THeory' and you find earth bound there.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthbound describes thinking that is prosaic and unimaginative, never soaring.

clue.text: Melvyn has skill — one with something to boast about

definitions.text: one with something to boast about

parts.note: Melvyn Bragg is a British broadcaster and novelist
skill means art

explanation.surface: A celebrated presenter has talent and plenty to show off about.
explanation.definitionFit: A braggart is a boaster, one who brags.

clue.text: See 8
Money left is collected by leader of girls

indicators.note: collected by something means gathered inside it

parts.note: a Guider is an adult leader in the Girl Guides

explanation.surface: A Guide leader collects the leftover cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The guilder was the currency of the Netherlands before the euro.

clue.text: Maybe automates newspaper department, leading to misfortunes

parts.note: a desk is a section of a newspaper office, such as the news desk
ills are troubles, misfortunes

explanation.surface: Newspaper bosses bring in automation, and bad luck follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To deskill a job is to remove the need for skilled labour, which automation does.

clue.text: No holy person takes alcoholic drink as a remedy

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A non-saint turns to drink as a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a patent medicine or quack cure.

clue.text: School performer entertains the French historian in the United States

parts.note: le is French for the
a singer is a performer

explanation.surface: A school musician hosts the French at an American history event.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Schlesinger Jr was a noted American historian and Kennedy adviser.

clue.text: Small creature squirted poison briefly, then died

indicators.note: squirted means sprayed out in a messy jumble, so the letters are rearranged
briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A tiny animal sprayed venom quickly and then perished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts POISON to POISO; 'squirted' rearranges it as ISOPO.
explanation.definitionFit: An isopod is a small crustacean such as a woodlouse.

clue.text: See 4
See 7
Plant is given washing, litres being shifted

indicators.note: shifted means moved to another position within the word

parts.note: ablution is the act of washing

explanation.surface: A houseplant gets watered, with a few litres splashed about.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the L of ABLUTION three places later gives the plant's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Abutilon is a flowering shrub of the mallow family, also called flowering maple.

clue.text: Picture of Hebrew leader

definitions.meaning: an image made of small tiles
relating to Moses, who led the Israelites

explanation.surface: An image depicting the man who led the Israelites.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosaic is a tiled picture; Mosaic also means pertaining to Moses, as in Mosaic law.

clue.text: Charles II, say, hugging his mistress and sounding mournful

parts.note: Charles II is an example of a king
Nell Gwyn was the mistress of Charles II

explanation.surface: The Restoration monarch embraces his favourite as a bell tolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Knelling describes a bell tolling for a death, a mournful sound.

clue.text: Part of Greater Manchester — an extra bit?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., something added as an extra fitting

explanation.surface: A town near Manchester as an add-on.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolton is a Greater Manchester town; a bolt-on is an accessory added to something.
